check.reason: The target is UnitedHealth, an insurer, which is squarely the system. No patients, reporters or private individuals are mocked. The satirical headline matches the real story, a lawsuit over downgraded Medicare Advantage quality scores. There are no invented figures or quotes, and 'billions at stake' is a general characterization of star-rating payments, not a specific number. The story involves no death, children or violence. The tone is dry and deadpan, and the joke is real satire: the insurer values quality measurement only when the scores favor it.

pick.title: UnitedHealth sues to reverse downgraded Medicare Advantage quality scores
pick.headline: UnitedHealth Sues Federal Government for Underrating Its Commitment to Quality
pick.take: With billions at stake, the insurer has found a deep faith in quality measurement, provided the measurements come out well. When the stars drop, the remedy is a lawsuit. Quality, it turns out, is whatever pays out after the appeal.
